DILG • Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph OILG OPINION NO. MR. ADRIAN CABILES CARPIO Charter President JC1-Sto. Tomas Batangas Dear Mr. Carpio: S. 20m This has reference to your letter dated 25 September 2019, requesting for the Department's legal opinion on the following: ii. iii. iv. v. vi. As a losing candidate, can he be appointed as councilor despite the one (I) year prohibition provided under RA No. 7160, or the Local Government Code 9LGC). Would it be possible for the Local Chief Executive not to appoint any councilors until such time that the one-year prohibition has lifted? Would it be possible for a term sharing set up for councilors? Can the Governor decide on the appointment instead of the City Mayor pursuant to Section 45 of the LGC? What are the legal grounds that Mayor will face for appointing these councilors in consideration of with/without legal bases? Any consideration from any national concerned agencies to reconsider the request in giving the Mayor the sole discretion on this matter especially from •municipality to city? Then Municipality of Sto. Tomas, Batangas has been converted into a city pursuant to Republic Act No. 11086, otherwise known as "AN ACT CONVERTING THE MUNICIPALITY OF STO. TOMAS IN THE PROVINCE OF BATANGAS INTO A COMPONENT CITY TO BE KNOWN AS THE cny OF STO. TOMAS". Section 10 thereof provides that there should be ten (10) regular Sangguniang Panlungsod members. Nevertheless, the then Municipality of Sto. Tomas have only 8 members, thus, there are two more members that should be appointed as members thereof. Per your letter, you are asking to be considered as one of the appointees to the membership of the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) of Sto. Tomas City in recognition for your active role in the youth sector and local community, albeit a losing candidate in the previous elections. Foremost, Section 94(b) of Republic Act (RA) No. 7160 or the Local Government Code (LGC) is very explicit that except for losing candidates in Barangay elections, no candidate who lost in any election shall, within one (1) year after such election, be appointed to any office in the government or any

government-owned or -controlled corporations or in any Of their subsidiaries. It can be gleaned thereon that only losing candidate in barangay elections is eligible to be appointed to any office in the government. Hence, query number I should be answered in the negative. With respect to your query numbers 2 and 3, Section 52 of RA No. 11086 categorically states that: "Section 52. Officials of the City of Sto. Tomas. - The present elective officials of the Municipality of Sto. Tomas shall continue to exercise their powers and functions until such time that a new election is held and the duly elected officials shall have already qualified and assumed their offices. The two (2) additional members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod shall be appointed by the City Mayor and shall assume office until such time that the regular members of the Sangguniang Pan/ungsod have been elected and qualified in the next national and local elections after the effectivity of this Act. Appointive officials and employees of the municipality shall likewise continue exercising their functions and duties and they shall be automatically absorbed by the city government of the City of Sto. Tomas. " It is being emphasized herein that the afore-quoted provision uses the word "shall" which is of a mandatory nature, wherein, the City Mayor is mandated to appoint the two (2) additional members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP). The two (2) additional appointees shall assume office until such time that the regular members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod have been elected and qualified in the next national and local elections after the effectivity of RA No. 11086. In view thereof, this level believes that the appointment should be made the soonest as the same involves public service which should not be delayed, and there can be no sharing of term as the law is very clear that the two (2) appointees shall assume office until regular member thereof have been elected and qualified. Likewise, we answer in the negative query number four. There is no conflict between Section 45(a)(2) of the LGC and Section 52 of RA No. 11086. The former pertains to the appointment by the governor when a permanent vacancy arises in the SP. On the other hand, in the latter, there is no permanent vacancy to speak of, but the appointees will be in addition to the existing membership of the SP because of the conversion from municipality to city, where, there is a need to increase the membership thereof. The said additional appointees is not due to permanent vacancy. Further, the requirement that the appointee shall come from the same political party as that of the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy is not applicable in the case at hand as this is not a vacancy referred to under Section 45(b) of the LGC. Accordingly, the legal basis of the Mayor in appointing the two (2) additional members of the SP is Section 52 of RA No. 11086.

As regards the last question, this Department is not the proper forum to address your request, in reconsidering the Mayor's sole discretion to appoint the additional members of the SP. The same should be threshed out with the courts of law. We hope we have addressed your concern sufficiently. Ve trul ours, E AR o Secr ary CC: Dir. Elias F. Fernandez Regional Director DILG-Region IV-A (CALABARZON) DILG-0SEc
